sections.h2: Which office bills a Macon property owner?
sections.html:
The Macon-Bibb County Tax Commissioner sends the bill, and what it collects is passed to the State of Georgia, Macon-Bibb County and the Board of Education. Millage rates come from the county's commissioners and the Bibb County school board, while the Tax Assessors determine values.

  • Tax Commissioner: phone 478-621-6500, email taxinfo@maconbibb.us, website maconbibbtax.us. It bills, collects, distributes the money and prepares the digest for the state each year.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: 688 Walnut Street, Suite 200, Macon, GA 31201, phone (478) 200-5550, website bibbassessors.com.
  • Deed room at the Macon-Bibb County Courthouse, 601 Mulberry St., for copies of a warranty deed.

The tax commissioner's FAQ stresses that the office is an independent elected one, separate from the assessors and from the county commissioners. Send value questions to the assessors and payment questions to the commissioner.

sections.h2: How does the Macon-Bibb housing picture compare with other Georgia counties?
sections.html:
Macon-Bibb County has the biggest population of the four Georgia places compared here, an estimated 157,556 in mid-2025. Against the 157,358 estimates base for 2020, that is a gain of just 0.1%.

With a land area of 249.38 square miles and a 2020 density of 630.9, Macon-Bibb is far more crowded than Lowndes, Lumpkin or Long County. Owners live in 51.4% of homes, the lowest share of the group, and the midpoint price of those homes is $174,500 in the 2020 through 2024 data. Renters pay $1,066 a month at the median, and the county has 59,921 households.

Half of households bring in less than $51,234, and 24.7% of residents fall below the poverty line. Retail sales in 2022 totaled about $5.87 billion, or $37,595 per resident, the highest by a wide margin of the four places, and medical and social service receipts came to roughly $2.45 billion.

sections.h2: What dates matter on a Macon property tax bill?
sections.html:
Macon-Bibb splits the bill on land, buildings and personal property into two installments. Weekend dates slide to Monday or the next business day.

Macon-Bibb County property tax calendar from the tax commissioner and the assessors
ItemDate or rule
Real and personal property statements mailedBy September 15
First installment dueOctober 15
Second installment dueNovember 15
Property returnsFiled by April 1
Homestead applicationReceived before April 1 to apply that year
Mobile home statements mailedBy January 30
Mobile home tax dueApril 1
Garbage fee, quarterlyMarch 31, June 30, September 30, December 31

Source: the tax commissioner's property and FAQ pages, plus the assessors' return deadline page.

A postal-service postmark with a date shows a current-year payment was on time. A date from a postage meter does not qualify. Partial payments are accepted, but penalties and interest keep running on the remainder. Millage rates are announced each year in late July or early August, once the commissioners and the Board of Education approve them.

sections.h2: Why is a garbage fee tied to Macon property tax?
sections.html:
Every residential premises meant for occupancy, vacant or not, is billed for garbage service, and the Solid Waste Department's service is mandatory. The tax commissioner's page says garbage is now billed quarterly, with due dates at the end of each quarter.

  • Appealing a property value does not pause the garbage fee, which stays due in full.
  • Owners with income under the federal poverty guidelines may seek an exemption, with with applications turned in at the Solid Waste Department, 327 Lower Poplar St., before the 5:00 p.m. cutoff on November 1 of each year.
  • If a home is destroyed by fire or casualty or demolished, the owner must tell the Solid Waste Director in writing immediately.

Solid Waste handles service questions at 478.803.0499 or garbage@maconbibb.us. Ask the commissioner whether a garbage charge is open when you request a payoff.

sections.h2: How do returns, homestead and appeals work for a Macon owner?
sections.html:
To get a value review, an owner has to file a return by April 1. The assessors say skipping it blocks any review. Returns go to the Tax Assessors' Office, which mails a notice when it disagrees with your figure.

A dispute must start 45 days or fewer after the notice date. The written appeal goes first to the Board of Assessors and has to name the method you choose. Call the assessors before you file if you are unsure how to proceed.

Homestead applications are approved by the Tax Assessors' Office. Eligibility turns on January 1: you need to be the owner and the resident that day. An application in hand before April 1 counts for that year, and a move or a deed change calls for a fresh one. Mobile home owners who dispute the assessed value get 45 days from the bill's mailing or until April 1, whichever is later.

sections.h2: What happens if Macon property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Tax unpaid after the due date is delinquent and carries interest and penalties set by state law. A 30-day notice of intent goes out before any lien (FiFa) is issued, and paying in full within that window avoids it. Mobile homes paid late face a state-mandated penalty of 10 percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, plus monthly interest.

  • Sales happen at 11 AM on the courthouse steps at the United Building in Central City Park, 206 7th Street, on the first Tuesday of any month with a sale on the calendar.
  • The winning bidder buys a Sheriff's Tax Deed, pays within two hours, and can use cash, certified funds or money orders only.
  • The owner can redeem within 12 months, and the price can include the bid, taxes the buyer paid afterward, special assessments and a 20% premium.
  • A buyer cannot foreclose the right to redeem before a year has passed since the sale.

Money left after a sale beyond taxes and costs, called excess funds, is held by the commissioner. A mortgage company or lienholder may claim it before the owner, and the page says competing claims can end up in Superior Court.

sections.h2: What follows a Macon-Bibb tax sale for the old owner and the buyer?
sections.html:
A sale list, when one is scheduled, runs in The Telegraph's legal advertisements every Tuesday for four weeks beforehand. Anyone curious about a delinquent property that is not on a list can ask for the Levy Department at 478-621-6500. The opening bid is the tax due plus penalties and fees, and extra costs for title research and advertising are added once a property is picked for sale.

The winning bidder holds a Sheriff's Tax Deed rather than a clean title, and Georgia law bars the buyer from taking possession, making improvements or evicting tenants right away. To cut off the owner's right to redeem once the 12 months pass, the buyer has to send certified mail to the record owner and every interest holder, then run a newspaper notice weekly for four straight weeks. A quiet title petition comes next, and the court appoints a Special Master to decide who was owed notice.

The county itself does not help with redemption or foreclosure of that right, so an owner facing a sale should seek professional advice quickly.

sections.h2: How does selling a Macon house with tax due work?
sections.html:
The commissioner bills the January 1 owner, or the current owner when the office hears of a transfer 90 days or fewer before the due date. Ownership data comes from deeds recorded at the courthouse and relayed by the assessors.

If you close between billing and the due dates, ask the commissioner at 478-621-6500 for a payoff that covers both installments. Lenders with escrow accounts get a data file, yet the owner stays responsible for making sure the tax is paid.

Boats, aircraft and business equipment work the same way: the January 1 owner owes the full year, even after a sale or a move out of the county, and the assessors want proof before they remove the account.

faqs.q: Which installment dates apply to Macon property tax?
faqs.a: October 15 and November 15, after statements are mailed by September 15. A weekend date moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Macon tax office?
faqs.a: The Macon-Bibb County Tax Commissioner answers at 478-621-6500. For value questions, the Board of Tax Assessors lists (478) 200-5550 on its own site.

faqs.q: Does Macon accept postmarks on mailed property tax payments?
faqs.a: Yes, but only a dated postal-service postmark counts toward the current year's tax, not a meter stamp.

faqs.q: When is the Macon homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: The office needs it before April 1 for it to count that year, and you have to hold and occupy the home on January 1.

faqs.q: When are Macon-Bibb tax sales held?
faqs.a: At 11 AM on the first Tuesday of a month with a sale scheduled, on the steps at the United Building in Central City Park. A bidder or representative has to be present.
